holidays.name: National Jelly Bean Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the small, chewy, brightly colored candy in every flavor, from classic cherry to buttered popcorn. Pour a bowl, sort them by color, and see whether you can pick out the weird flavors.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its exact origin is unclear. It lands in the Easter season, when jelly beans are at their most popular.
holidays.funFact: A jelly bean takes about a week to make. Most of that time goes into building up the shell, which is layered on in a process called panning.

holidays.name: April Showers Day
holidays.description: A salute to the rainy weather that gives spring its reputation. Splash in puddles, break out the umbrella and rain boots, and remember that the rain is what makes the flowers grow.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the old saying that April rain brings May flowers.
holidays.funFact: The proverb about April showers and May flowers goes back centuries in English. A version of it appears in Thomas Tusser's 16th-century farming verses.

holidays.name: Global Selfie Earth Day
holidays.description: An Earth Day twist where people snap selfies outdoors with nature, then share them to show they care about the planet. Use it as a reason to get outside, pick up litter, and take a photo with a tree.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It pairs the modern selfie habit with the environmental message of Earth Day.
holidays.funFact: The word "selfie" was named Oxford Dictionaries' Word of the Year in 2013.
